newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Hoechst disappoints investors with HMR news.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hoechst disappoints investors with HMR news.

text.p: German drugs and chemicals group Hoechst AG on Wednesday stunned financial markets by shelving plans to float its drugs unit HMR while insisting there had been no change in overall strategy.

Investors punished Hoechst for both weaker than expected results and confirmation that the group no longer planned to seek a separate bourse listing for HMR by sending shares into a freefall, dropping as much as 12 percent in bourse trade.
Hoechst's shares closed bourse trade down 8.10 marks at 70.45 marks while the DAX fell just 1.31 percent to 3,415.40.

"We see bringing HMR to the stock market as no longer being in the best interests of our shareholders," Hoechst chairman Juergen Dormann told analysts, stressing however "this should not be seen as a change in our strategy".

At a news conference Dormann elaborated that Hoechst was eager to keep the drugs group, which has tremendous growth potential, within the Hoechst group in order to better sieze possible merger or takeover opportunities.

One day earlier Hoechst announced its 1996 sales had dropped two percent to 50.9 billion marks ($29.8 billion) while pre-tax profit, driven largely by income from spin-offs, had climbed 29 percent to 5.28 billion marks. Hoechst also revealed a 383 million mark loss in the fourth quarter, which caught analysts off guard.
"The outlook is not that great and I think we will see forecasts reduced," said Tony Cox, analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in London.
Gone now are the heady days when Hoechst last November managed to delight investors by offsetting weak nine-month operating results with news it planned to list its shares in New York this October.
Talk that HMR would be floated sometime after the Hoechst AG New York listing had been circulating for nearly one year.
But analysts now spoke of damaged credibility and loss of trust while traders complained that by distancing itself from the HMR listing, Hoechst had dealt them "a slap in the face".
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell downgraded Hoechst to neutral from overweight and another analyst said, "You are not going to see anyone running out to buy this company any time soon."

In efforts to keep market interest alive, Hoechst board members ticked off ambitious plans, including the possible sale of the generic drugs business and plans to spin off its diagnostics business into a joint-venture with U.S. Dade International.
A bourse listing is planned for Dade Behring, but Dormann stepped clear of questions about possible other flotations saying nothing concrete was planned at the moment.

To keep the market interest alive, Hoechst focused on future plans saying it might consider selling its struggling generics drugs business and would move its diagnostics group Behring Diagnostics into a joint venture with U.S. group Dade International.

Dormann also said the first quarter 1997 had gotten off to a good start, saying "we are anticpating favourable business developments due to lively volume demand, an increase in prices in the industrial sector," and the benefits of a strong dollar.

He predicted that 1997's operating profit would be near year-ago levels but warned against comparisons with 1996's 4.013 billion mark profit as this number still reflects units that were spun off last year.

But the mood was nonetheless palpably critical as journalists repeatedly demanded that Dormann explain how he was able to sound a relatively optimistic tone in November of 1996 only to be surprised by some 400 million marks in restructuring costs and costs for product recalls weeks later.
Hoechst also sought to showcase its pharmaceuticals division boasting a 217 percent rise in 1996 operating profit to 2.249 billion marks and a 20 percent rise in sales to 13.020 billion marks.
The group also said it was working hard on filling its pipeline and expected to have new launches of key drugs in a short time.
Hoechst cut is workforce by 8.5 percent last year and still expected to trim more jobs this year.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.708 German Marks)
